state.persona: Traveler in Monaco on a phone (390x844) who saw a yacht opportunity and wants to pursue it.
state.jtbd: Open the Monaco yacht offer and ask about it.
state.before_action: They scrolled ~1250px down the ACCESS list and see a card: 'YACHT / BOAT · AVAILABILITY BY REQUEST · Harbor morning, race week · Port Hercules · A berth-adjacent morning on the water... Inquiry only. · Riviera Deck · On request · [REQUEST DETAILS button]'.
state.what_happens: The URL changes to /access?offer=opp-monaco-harbor and the page jumps to the very top. The first viewport after the tap is pixel-identical to the ACCESS landing view: hero photo, 'MERIDIAN / ACCESS', 'Make the trip happen.', 'Explore opportunities ↘', 'Place archive photography · preview opportunities, not live inventory', then the disclosure 'Sample partner opportunities for product preview. Nothing here is live inventory or a confirmed reservation.' and '01 / DISCOVER'. The new section 'YOUR SELECTED POSSIBILITY' with the chosen offer begins about 1460px down the page (below the hero, disclosure and a three-step explainer). No toast, no scroll to the offer, no visual change above the fold.

notices_selection.instructions: Would this traveler, looking only at the first viewport after the tap, realise their tap selected the offer and that details are further down?

criteria.false: No, likely thinks nothing happened or the page reset

perceived_outcome.instructions: What will the traveler most likely conclude right after the tap?

criteria.reset: The page reloaded / nothing happened / something broke
criteria.request_sent: A request for details was sent to the provider
criteria.details_below: The details opened lower on the page

label_predicts.instructions: Does the label 'REQUEST DETAILS' on a sample, non-live offer correctly predict an in-page detail view that sends nothing to anyone?

criteria.false: Label implies a request is sent / something else
